html:
In the Winter War the Soviet Union invaded Finland on 30 November 1939. The Finns held out for three and a half months before making peace in March 1940.

Stalin demanded land near Leningrad and a naval base. When Finland refused, the Red Army attacked with far more men, tanks and planes. Finnish troops on skis, in white camouflage, cut off and destroyed Soviet columns in the forests, and the Mannerheim Line on the Karelian Isthmus held for weeks. Petrol bombs thrown at tanks were nicknamed Molotov cocktails.

In the end Finland had to give up about a tenth of its territory, including Vyborg and much of Karelia, and over 400,000 people were evacuated. But it stayed independent. The war showed the weakness of the Red Army and led to the Continuation War. See Finland and the Second World War.
sum: In the Winter War the Soviet Union invaded Finland on 30 November 1939. The Finns held out for three and a half months before making peace in March 1940.
